source_text:
Uideamus igitur, quid me doceat Manichaeus, et potissimum illum consideremus librum, quem Fundamenti epistulam dicitis, ubi totum paene, quod creditis, continetur. ipsa enim nobis illo tempore miseris quando lecta est, inluminati dicebamur a uobis. certe sic incipit: Manichaeus apostolus
Iesu Christi prouidentia dei patris. haec sunt salubria uerba de perenni ac uiuo fonte. iam cum bona patientia, si placet, adtendite, quid quaeram. non credo esse istum apostolum Christi. quaeso, ne suscenseatis et male dicere incipiatis. nostis enim me statuisse nihil a uobis prolatum temere credere. quaero ergo, quis sit iste Manichaeus. respondebitis: apostolus Christi. non credo; quid iam dicas aut facias, non habebis. promittebas enim scientiam ueritatis, et nunc quod nescio cogis, ut credam. euangelium mihi fortasse lecturus es et inde Manichaei personam temptabis adserere. si ergo inuenires aliquem, qui euangelio nondum credit, quid faceres dicenti tibi: non credo? ego uero euangelio non crederem, nisi me catholicae ecclesiae conmoueret auctoritas.I quibus ergo obtemperaui dicentibus: crede euangelio, cur eis non obtemperem dicentibus mihi: noli credere Manichaeis ? elige, quid uelis. si dixeris: crede catholicis, ipsi me monent, ut nullam fidem adcommodem uobis; quapropter non possum illis credens nisi tibi non credere. si dixeris: noli catholicis credere, non recte facies per euangelium me cogere ad Manichaei fidem, quia ipsi euangelio catholicis praedicantibus credidi. si autem dixeris: recte credidisti catholicis laudantibus euangelium, sed non recte illis credidisti uituperantibus Manichaeum, usque adeo me stultum putas, ut nulla reddita ratione, quod uis credam, quod non uis. non credam? multo enim iustius atque cautius facio, si catholicis quoniam semel credidi, ad te non transeo, nisi me non credere iusseris, sed apertissime ac manifestissime scire aliquid feceris. quocirca si mihi rationem redditurus es. dimitte euangelium. si ad euangelium te tenes, ego me ad eos teneam, quibus praecipientibus euangelio credidi, et his iubentibus tibi omnino non credam. quodsi forte in euangelio aliquid apertissimum de Manichaei apostolatu inuenire potueris, infirmabis mihi catholicorum auctoritatem, qui iubent, ut tibi non credam: qua infirmata iam nec euangelio credere potero. quia per eos illi credideram. ita nihil apud me ualebit, quicquid inde protuleris. quapropter si nihil manifestum de Manichaei apostolatu in euangelio reperitur, catholicis potius credam quam tibi. si autem aliquid inde manifestum pro Manichaeo legeris, nec illis nec tibi: illis, quia de te mihi mentiti sunt; tibi autem. quia eam scripturam mihi profers, cui per illos credideram, qui mihi mentiti sunt. sed absit. ut euangelio ego non credam. illi enim credens non inuenio, quomodo possim etiam tibi credere; apostolorum enim nomina, quae ibi leguntur. non inter se continent nomen Manichaei. in locum autem traditoris Christi quis successerit, in apostolorum actibus legimus: cui libro necesse est me credere, si credo euangelio. quoniam utramque scripturam similiter mihi catholica commendat auctoritas. in eodem etiam libro de uocatione atque apostolatu Pauli uulgatissimam tenemus historiam. lege mihi iam, si potes, in euangelio, ubi Manichaeus apostolus dictus est, uel in aliquo alio libro, cui me iam credidisse confiteor. an illud lecturus es, ubi spiritum sanctum paracletum dominus promisit apostolis ? de quo loco uide, quot et quanta sint, quae me reuocent et deterreant, ne Manichaeo credam.
thought_title: Why Augustine will not believe Mani without proof
orientation: Augustine has just recalled how he was called 'illuminated' when Mani's Fundamental Letter was read to him, and now he begins to test Mani's claim to be an apostle of Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Let us see therefore what Mani teaches me, and especially let us consider that book which you call the Letter of the Foundation, where almost everything that you believe is contained. For when that very letter was read to us at that time, we wretched ones were said by you to be illuminated. Certainly it begins thus: Mani, apostle of Jesus Christ by the providence of God the Father. These are the wholesome words from the perennial and living fountain. Now with good patience, if you please, attend to what I am asking. I do not believe that this man is an apostle of Christ. I ask you not to be angry and begin to speak evil. For you know that I have decided to believe nothing rashly that is brought forward by you. I ask therefore who this Mani is. You will answer: an apostle of Christ. I do not believe; what you may now say or do, you will not have. For you were promising knowledge of the truth, and now you force me to believe what I do not know. Perhaps you are going to read the gospel to me and from it you will try to assert the person of Mani. If therefore you should find someone who does not yet believe the gospel, what would you do to him saying to you: I do not believe? I for my part would not believe the gospel unless the authority of the Catholic Church moved me. Those therefore whom I obeyed when they said: believe the gospel, why should I not obey them when they say to me: do not believe the Manichaeans? Choose what you wish. If you say: believe the Catholics, they themselves warn me to give no faith to you; wherefore I cannot, believing them, do anything but not believe you. If you say: do not believe the Catholics, you will not rightly do to force me through the gospel to faith in Mani, because I believed the gospel itself when the Catholics preached it. But if you say: you rightly believed the Catholics when they praised the gospel, but you did not rightly believe them when they blamed Mani, do you think me so foolish that, with no reason given, I should believe what you wish and not believe what you do not wish? For I act much more justly and cautiously if, since I once believed the Catholics, I do not pass over to you, unless you order me not to believe, but make me know something most openly and most clearly. Wherefore if you are going to give me a reason, put aside the gospel. If you hold to the gospel, I hold to those by whose instruction I believed the gospel, and at their command I will not believe you at all. But if perhaps you can find in the gospel something most open about the apostleship of Mani, you will weaken for me the authority of the Catholics, who command that I not believe you; and when that authority is weakened, I will no longer be able to believe the gospel either, because through them I had believed it. Thus whatever you bring forth from it will have no force with me. Wherefore if nothing clear about the apostleship of Mani is found in the gospel, I will rather believe the Catholics than you. But if you read something clear from it on behalf of Mani, I will believe neither them nor you: not them, because they lied to me about you; not you, because you bring me that scripture which I had believed through them, who lied to me. But far be it that I should not believe the gospel. For believing it, I do not find how I could also believe you; for the names of the apostles, which are read there, do not contain among themselves the name of Mani. But who succeeded in the place of the betrayer of Christ, we read in the Acts of the Apostles; and I must believe that book if I believe the gospel, since the Catholic authority commends both scriptures to me alike. In the same book also we hold the very well-known history of the calling and apostleship of Paul. Read to me now, if you can, in the gospel where Mani is called an apostle, or in any other book which I confess I have already believed. Or are you going to read that passage where the Lord promised the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, to the apostles? About that passage, see how many and how great are the things that call me back and deter me from believing Mani.

choices.why: The work's title in the brief is 'the Letter of Mani Called Fundamental'; rendering the Latin literally as 'Letter of the Foundation' preserves the source wording while matching the brief's title.

choices.english: by the providence of God the Father
choices.why: Literal rendering of the ablative phrase; 'providence' is the standard English for 'prouidentia' and keeps the theological sense.
rejected: through the foresight of God the Father

choices.term: salubria uerba de perenni ac uiuo fonte
choices.english: wholesome words from the perennial and living fountain
choices.why: Literal translation preserving the metaphor and the adjectives 'perennial' and 'living' as in the source.
rejected: healing words from the ever-flowing and living spring
sound words from the eternal and living source

choices.why: Literal rendering; 'knowledge' is the standard English for 'scientia' and the phrase is central to Augustine's critique of Mani's promise.

choices.english: the authority of the Catholic Church moved me
choices.why: Literal word order and sense; 'Catholic Church' is the brief's required rendering for 'catholica ecclesia'.
rejected: the Catholic Church's authority moved me
the authority of the universal Church moved me

choices.why: Standard English for 'apostolatus'; keeps the noun form parallel to the source.

bible_refs.note: Augustine refers to the successor chosen in the place of Judas the betrayer, which is narrated in Acts 1:26.
Augustine refers to the well-known history of Paul's calling and apostleship, narrated in Acts 9.
Augustine refers to the Lord's promise of the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, to the apostles.

pass_b_english: Let us see, then, what Mani teaches me, and let us look especially at that book you call the Letter of the Foundation, where almost everything you believe is contained. Indeed, when it was read to us in that wretched time, you told us we were illuminated. It certainly begins like this: “Mani, apostle of Jesus Christ by the providence of God the Father. These are wholesome words from the perennial and living fountain.” Now, with good patience, if you please, pay attention to what I am asking. I do not believe that this man is an apostle of Christ. Please do not be angry and start speaking harshly. You know that I have resolved to believe nothing rashly that you bring forward. So I ask: who is this Mani? You will answer: an apostle of Christ. I do not believe it; and now you will have nothing left to say or do. You were promising knowledge of the truth, and now you are forcing me to believe what I do not know. Perhaps you are about to read me the gospel and try to establish Mani’s identity from it. But if you found someone who did not yet believe the gospel, what would you do if he said to you, “I do not believe”? I myself would not believe the gospel unless the authority of the Catholic Church moved me.

So if I obeyed those who said to me, “Believe the gospel,” why should I not obey those who say to me, “Do not believe the Manichaeans”? Choose what you want. If you say, “Believe the Catholics,” they themselves warn me to give no faith to you; therefore, believing them, I cannot but not believe you. If you say, “Do not believe the Catholics,” you will not do rightly to force me through the gospel to Mani’s faith, because I believed the gospel itself when the Catholics preached it. But if you say, “You were right to believe the Catholics when they praised the gospel, but you were not right to believe them when they blamed Mani,” do you think me so foolish that, with no reason given, I should believe what you want and not believe what you reject? I act far more justly and cautiously if, since I once believed the Catholics, I do not come over to you unless you order me not to believe them, but make me know something most openly and clearly. Therefore, if you are going to give me a reason, set the gospel aside. If you hold to the gospel, I will hold to those at whose command I believed the gospel, and at their command I will not believe you at all. But if by chance you can find something in the gospel most clear about Mani’s apostleship, you will weaken for me the authority of the Catholics, who command me not to believe you; and once that authority is weakened, I will no longer be able to believe the gospel either, because it was through them that I believed it. So whatever you bring forward from it will have no weight with me. Therefore, if nothing clear about Mani’s apostleship is found in the gospel, I will believe the Catholics rather than you. But if you read something clear from it in Mani’s favor, I will believe neither them nor you: not them, because they lied to me about you; and not you, because you are offering me the very Scripture I believed through them, and they lied to me. But far be it from me not to believe the gospel. For believing it, I do not find how I can also believe you; the names of the apostles that are read there do not include the name of Mani among them. And who succeeded in the place of Christ’s betrayer we read in the Acts of the Apostles; and I must believe that book if I believe the gospel, since the Catholic authority commends both Scriptures to me alike. In that same book we also have the well-known history of Paul’s calling and apostleship. Read to me now, if you can, where in the gospel Mani is called an apostle, or in any other book that I confess I have already believed. Or will you read the passage where the Lord promised the apostles the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete? Look at that passage and see how many and how great are the things that call me back and deter me from believing Mani.

problems.quote: I cannot do anything but not believe you
problems.source_quote: non possum illis credens nisi tibi non credere
problems.why: 'Nisi' with infinitive means 'except to not believe you,' i.e., 'I cannot believe them without not believing you.'
problems.fix: believing them, I cannot but not believe you

problems.quote: you will not rightly use the gospel to force me
problems.source_quote: non recte facies per euangelium me cogere
problems.why: 'Facies' = 'you will do/act,' not 'use'; 'per evangelium' = 'through the gospel,' not instrumental 'use.'
problems.fix: you will not rightly act to force me through the gospel

problems.quote: unless you do not merely order me to believe
problems.why: 'Non credere iusseris' = 'unless you order me not to believe' — absurd; should be 'nisi me... scire aliquid feceris' with 'non credere' as error in English reading.
problems.fix: unless you make me know something
problems.ruling: 'nisi me non credere iusseris' = 'unless you order me not to believe'; English 'do not merely order' mistranslates the Latin.

problems.quote: we read in the Acts of the Apostles (Acts 1:26)
problems.why: Augustine does not give chapter-verse; modern citation added by translator without brackets.
problems.fix: we read in the Acts of the Apostles
problems.ruling: Source 'in apostolorum actibus legimus' has no chapter-verse; '(Acts 1:26)' added without brackets misleads readers.

problems.why: Same issue: Augustine gives no reference; translator adds Acts 9:1-19 without indication.
problems.ruling: Source 'de vocatione atque apostolatu Pauli' has no reference; '(Acts 9:1-19)' added without brackets misleads readers.

problems.why: Same issue: no Johannine reference in source; translator adds John 14:16.
problems.ruling: Source 'spiritum sanctum paracletum' has no Johannine reference; '(John 14:16)' added without brackets misleads readers.

edits.old: believing them, I cannot do anything but not believe you
edits.new: believing them, I cannot but not believe you

edits.old: you will not rightly use the gospel to force me to Mani’s faith
edits.new: you will not rightly act to force me through the gospel to Mani’s faith

edits.old: I do not come over to you unless you do not merely order me to believe, but make me know something most openly and clearly
edits.new: I do not come over to you unless you make me know something most openly and clearly

edits.old: we read in the Acts of the Apostles (Acts 1:26)
edits.new: we read in the Acts of the Apostles

fixed: Corrected 'I cannot do anything but not believe you' to 'I cannot but not believe you' to reflect 'nisi tibi non credere' as 'except to not believe you.'
Corrected 'you will not rightly use the gospel to force me' to 'you will not rightly act to force me through the gospel' to reflect 'non recte facies per euangelium me cogere.'
Corrected 'unless you do not merely order me to believe' to 'unless you make me know something' to reflect 'nisi me... scire aliquid feceris.'
Removed added citation '(Acts 1:26)' not present in source.
Removed added citation '(Acts 9:1-19)' not present in source.
Removed added citation '(John 14:16)' not present in source.

problems.quote: I should believe what you want and not believe what you do not want
problems.source_quote: quod uis credam, quod non uis. non credam
problems.why: The second "non uis" governs "non credam": "what you do not want, I should not believe" — the English makes it sound like Augustine is choosing, but the Latin is a rhetorical question about Mani's arbitrary demands.
problems.fix: I should believe what you want and not believe what you do not want me to?

edits.old: I should believe what you want and not believe what you do not want?
edits.new: I should believe what you want and not believe what you do not want me to?

fixed: The English already renders the rhetorical question correctly: 'I should believe what you want and not believe what you do not want?' The source 'quod uis credam, quod non uis. non credam' is a rhetorical question, and the English preserves that. No edit needed.

problems.quote: you will not rightly act to force me through the gospel to Mani's faith
problems.source_quote: non recte facies per euangelium me cogere ad Manichaei fidem
problems.why: Latin is simple future statement 'you will not do rightly', not conditional 'you will not rightly act'; changes from prediction to modal judgment.
problems.fix: you will not do rightly to force me through the gospel to Mani's faith

problems.quote: and not believe what you do not want me to
problems.why: The Latin is 'what you do not want, may I not believe it' (optative/subjunctive), not 'what you do not want me to [believe]'; Augustine asks not to believe what Mani doesn't want, i.e., the Catholics' warning.
problems.fix: and not believe what you reject
problems.ruling: 'quod non vis, non credam' = 'what you don't want, I won't believe'; English 'what you don't want me to' changes meaning.

problems.quote: unless you make me know something most openly and clearly
problems.source_quote: nisi me non credere iusseris, sed apertissime ac manifestissime scire aliquid feceris
problems.why: Missing 'non credere iusseris' (unless you order me not to believe [the Catholics]); the English skips the paradox of being ordered to disbelieve.
problems.fix: unless you order me not to believe them, but make me know something most openly and clearly
problems.ruling: Source has 'nisi me non credere iusseris' (unless you order me not to believe); English omits this key clause entirely.

edits.old: you will not rightly act to force me through the gospel to Mani’s faith
edits.new: you will not do rightly to force me through the gospel to Mani’s faith

edits.old: and not believe what you do not want me to?
edits.new: and not believe what you reject?

edits.old: I do not come over to you unless you make me know something most openly and clearly.
edits.new: I do not come over to you unless you order me not to believe them, but make me know something most openly and clearly.

fixed: Modality: source 'non recte facies' is simple future 'you will not do rightly', so changed to 'you will not do rightly to force me'.
Mistranslation: source 'quod non uis. non credam' is optative 'what you do not want, may I not believe it', so changed to 'and not believe what you reject'.
Mistranslation: source includes 'nisi me non credere iusseris' (unless you order me not to believe), so restored that clause.

dismissed.quote: you told us we were illuminated
dismissed.why: Passive 'dicebamur' means 'we were called/said to be illuminated,' not 'you told us.'
dismissed.note: 'You told us we were illuminated' is a fair, natural rendering of 'inluminati dicebamur a uobis'.

last_rejected.quote: when it was read to us in that wretched time
last_rejected.source_quote: nobis illo tempore miseris quando lecta est
last_rejected.why: miseris agrees with nobis: the hearers were wretched then, not the time.
last_rejected.fix: when it was read to us, wretched as we were at that time, you called us illuminated.
last_rejected.ruling: "nobis illo tempore miseris" — miseris agrees with nobis, so "wretched us at that time" is correct; but the English "in that wretched time" conveys the same wretchedness, a minor shift.

last_rejected.quote: unless you order me not to believe them, but make me know something
last_rejected.source_quote: nisi me non credere iusseris, sed apertissime ac manifestissime scire aliquid feceris
last_rejected.why: The source has no 'them'. The contrast is between being ordered to believe (blindly) and being made to know. The English makes it a command to stop believing the Catholics.
last_rejected.fix: unless you, instead of ordering me merely to believe, make me know something most openly and clearly
last_rejected.ruling: “non credere iusseris” is “order me not to believe”; “them” only supplies nearby “catholicis,” and “sed … scire feceris” is kept.
